title: Model Promotion Orchestrator: declarative canary knobs, shadow plumbing, and safe undo APIs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver an API + client libraries that let product and infra teams safely promote model versions through staged exposures (canary ramp, A/B allocations, shadowing) and automatically or manually undo changes when quality or reliability regressions are detected.

Scope:
- Server endpoints for CRUD of a 'promotion plan' (create, update traffic split, pause, resume, rollback, status).
- Declarative rollout spec supporting: time-based ramps, percent-based steps, A/B experiment binding, shadow routes, experiment metadata (owner, ticket, metric targets).
- Client SDK helpers (JS + Python) for transactional operations, idempotent create/update, and local simulation utilities for canary ramp scheduling.
- Idempotency: client-supplied X-Rollout-Idempotency-Key header; server dedup window 24h with at-least-once semantics for retry safety.
- Permission model: granular scopes (rollout.create, rollout.modify, rollout.view, rollout.rollback) and resource-level grants for customer accounts / projects.
- Auto-rollback triggers: composable rules that evaluate metrics from the Console telemetry pipeline (examples: error_rate increase >3x sustained 5m, p95 latency regress >20% with statistical significance).
- Observability: per-rollout metrics (exposed to Console and metric API): allocation-weighted latency/error, cohort-level histograms, drift/quality regressions, decision logs and audit entries for each traffic-change action.
- Safe defaults: conservative initial canary (1% for 30m), soft-fail policy (automatically pause ramp on transient anomalies but do not fully rollback unless escalation rules are met), and a kill-switch endpoint for immediate cutover.

API surface (examples):
- POST /v1/promotion_plans -> create new plan (idempotency via header).
- GET /v1/promotion_plans/{id} -> current spec + status + active allocations.
- PATCH /v1/promotion_plans/{id}/traffic -> atomically change weights (server validates permissions and quota).
- POST /v1/promotion_plans/{id}/actions: {"type":"pause|resume|rollback|force_cutover"}.
- POST /v1/promotion_plans/{id}/simulate -> run canary in dry-run against historical traffic to show expected exposures and metric impact.
- Webhook callback contract for external monitoring/alerting integrations when auto-rollback triggers or plan completes.

SDK primitives:
- createPromotion(plan, idempotencyKey, opts) -> returns plan record or existing record if deduped.
- watchPlan(planId, onUpdate) -> streaming updates for UI consoles.
- atomicUpdateTraffic(planId, setOps, opts) -> safe compare-and-swap helpers.
- simulateLocal(planSpec, sampleTraffic) -> local opt-in tool to preview exposures.

Operational constraints / decisions:
- Server will enforce a max single-step delta (e.g., cannot jump >20% allocation without an explicit force flag) to avoid blast radius.
- Idempotency keys are canonicalized per-account and retained for 24 hours; dedupe mechanism is single-record, then eventual reconciliation job tags duplicate attempts for audit.
- Default auto-rollback thresholds are configurable at org level; advanced customers can supply custom rules and tie to external evaluators.
- All rollout actions produce audit logs exportable to customer KMS-backed storage for Private deployments.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Full experiment analysis engine (we will integrate with the existing A/B telemetry pipeline in a follow-up).
- UI polish beyond basic Console surfaces (Console work is tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: API endpoints exist for create/get/patch/actions/simulate and follow the request/response contracts in the design doc
JS and Python SDKs have helpers for idempotent create and atomic traffic updates with unit tests
Server honors X-Rollout-Idempotency-Key semantics and persists dedupe state for 24 hours
RBAC enforced: rollout.create, rollout.modify, rollout.rollback, rollout.view scopes validated against customer projects
Auto-rollback rules can be created and attached to a promotion plan; simulated trigger causes a paused plan or rollback in staging
End-to-end integration test that runs a simulated canary and verifies telemetry is emitted to the metrics pipeline
Audit entries (user, action, timestamp, reason) generated for every manual or automatic state change and visible in Console and logs
Documentation (Confluence) with example SDK snippets, REST contract, and runbook for handling failed canaries
comments: 2026-02-11 - Maya Chen: Drafted initial product spec and high-level API surface; shared with Eng for feasibility check.
2026-02-18 - Arjun Patel (ENG): Reviewed; flagged complexity around cross-account idempotency and the need for a centralized dedupe store. Suggested 24h window and single-record dedupe strategy.
2026-02-25 - Design review: Console team asked for a streaming watchPlan hook to simplify UI state management; added to SDK primitives.

2026-03-03 - Security: Suggested RBAC scope names and noted audit export requirement for Private customers; security review not required for initial MVP config but will be gated for enterprise release.
2026-03-08 - Engineering: Implemented POST /v1/promotion_plans and basic persistence; opened PR #4389 (github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4389).

2026-03-10 - QA: Began writing integration tests for idempotency and permission checks; discovered race when two concurrent traffic updates attempt overlapping weight shifts. Follow-up spike assigned to ENG team.

2026-03-12 - PM decision: Default canary step set to 1% for 30m. Escalation policy: pause-on-anomaly for first breach, rollback only when consecutive breaches across two metrics occur within 10 minutes.
